newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Western economists urge economic reform on Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Western economists urge economic reform on Ukraine.

text.p: A leading Western economist urged Ukraine on Tuesday to approve a tax reform package and overdue budget quickly to achieve stability and growth.
"Ukraine needs more profound reform than originally expected," Anders Aslund, a director of the Soros International Economic Advisory Group, told a meeting of economists and government officials.
"The draft laws should be passed more quickly," he said.
Aslund said corruption, a punitive tax system and a high degree of regulation were impeding economic growth, forecast at zero this year after the economy shrank 10 percent in 1996.
The economist also said privatised enterprises required new executives to replace Soviet-era managers.
"Here we should act more promptly so reforms are more profound," Aslund said.
Parliament, dominated by conservative deputies, is reviewing the package of tax reforms which will underpin the budget. Under Ukraine's constitution the budget should have been passed by January 1.
Soros economist Marek Dabrowski said Ukraine needed to reform its generous system of social benefits and pension payments, which he said was the highest among former Soviet republics.

"Pensions have become the most important stumbling block for economic stabilisation," Dabrowski said, adding that many unemployed try to get the status of pensioners to receive some sort of government benefit.
